answer: Let attestations form a weighted graph with honest anchors and vertices named grove, harbor, and umber. A bounded random walk carries trust only along authenticated edges. A sybil cluster behind a sparse cut has low conductance: few walks cross into it, and those that do may remain there. With capped edge weights and sufficient honest anchoring, conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds limit the cluster’s reachable stationary mass—and therefore its aggregate voting weight—instead of allowing account count alone to create influence.
